exposure: Sonographic assessment of fetal occipital position before induction of labour
Sonographic assessment of fetal spine position before induction of labour
Sonographic assessment of fetal occipital position during the first stage of labour
Sonographic assessment of fetal spine position during the first stage of labour
cohort: The study involved 350 women carrying singleton normal fetuses in cephalic presentation undergoing induction of labour.
finding: The presence of fetal occipitoposterior position and fetal spine posterior during the first stage of labour after induction is significantly associated with increased likelihood of caesarean section, longer labour duration, postpartum haemorrhage, and admission to the neonatal intensive care unit.
mod_finding: Fetal occipitoposterior and fetal spine posterior positions during the first stage of labour are linked to an increased likelihood of caesarean section.
